title: Every countable Borel equivalence relation is hyperfinite on a comeagre invariant set

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the unlabelled theorem, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Countable Borel equivalence relation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Borel equivalence relation all of whose classes are countable, expressible as a countable union of graphs of Borel involutions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the relation whose restriction is shown to be hyperfinite.

standard_prerequisites.name: Hyperfinite relation
standard_prerequisites.statement: An equivalence relation is hyperfinite when it is the increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the property concluded on the restricted relation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Comeagre invariant set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A comeagre Borel set that is a union of classes, so that the restriction of the relation to it is still an equivalence relation.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the set produced by the construction.

core_obligations: Write the relation as a countable union of graphs of Borel involutions and use the enumeration to build a sequence of graphs whose powers generate larger and larger finite relations (source lines 669-671).
Fix a pairing bijection and a basis of the space, and for each index collect the basic open sets that are large in the corresponding finite graph, obtaining a comeagre set C' (source lines 671-674).
Remove the saturation of the complement of C' to obtain a comeagre invariant Borel set on which the relation is the increasing union of the finite relations, hence hyperfinite (source line 675).

proof_roadmap.step: Express the relation through Borel involutions and build the finite graphs.
Collect the large basic open sets into a comeagre set C'.
Make C' invariant and read off hyperfiniteness.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's unlabelled theorem at source lines 664-666: for a countable Borel equivalence relation on a Polish space there is a comeagre invariant Borel set on which the restriction of the relation is hyperfinite. The author gave it no label, so its position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 668-676) is a construction that the statement does not show: the relation is first written as a countable union of graphs of Borel involutions, which produces an increasing sequence of finite relations; a pairing bijection and a basis of the space are then used to collect, for every index, the basic open sets that are large in the corresponding finite graph, giving a comeagre set; finally the saturation of the complement is removed so that the resulting set is both comeagre and invariant, and on it the relation is the increasing union of the finite relations. The statement records only the existence of the set.
